about: Every number on these slides and in their speaker notes, with its source. All of them come from tasks we wrote, measured on October 29, 2026. The learning page, site/content/learning.json, uses the same numbers.

claims.number: Llama 3.2 1B and 3B, unchanged, on the same frozen 150-row test: exact match 12.0% and 52.0%; typed values written as strings in 8.3% and 17.5% of calls
claims.source: Tessera’s continuous-tuning record: the unchanged base models on the frozen, tool-call test we wrote. A typed value written as a string, such as a quoted number, makes a strict server reject the call.

claims.number: Muse Glimmer 30B, unchanged, on a fresh 150-row test: exact match 93.3%, valid JSON 96.7%
claims.source: The base model’s scores in the published run record, on a fresh, tool-call test we wrote whose hashes were registered before scoring.

claims.number: Frozen test: 150 rows over tool families held out of training
claims.source: Tessera’s continuous-tuning record: the test split holds the buckets and feeds tool families, pinned by digest, and training prompts only ever show other families. Each round also freezes a fresh holdout from the test families.

claims.number: Llama 3.2 1B, round 4: schema-augmented training lifted the development score from 61.25% to 76.25%, but the frozen test stayed at 50.7%; kept out
claims.source: The development set and the frozen test disagreed. The augmented adapter tied the champion on the test, while its schema validity fell to 61.7% and its false refusals rose to 17.5%, so the rule kept the champion.

claims.number: Llama 3.2 3B, round 2: 79.3% exact match, but schema validity fell 0.025 against a 0.02 limit; kept out
claims.source: The adapter scored above the champion, but the promotion rule, committed before any training round, allows schema validity to drop by at most 0.02, so the champion stayed.

claims.number: Muse Glimmer 30B with 63 training examples: +5.3 points on the frozen test, 95% CI 0.0 to +11.3; kept out
claims.source: The 63-row run on the frozen development test: exact match 87.3% to 92.7%, with 14 rows better and 6 worse. The paired bootstrap lower bound was not above zero, so the rule kept the base.

claims.number: Llama 3.2 1B, rounds 0 to 4 on the frozen, 150-row test we wrote: exact match 12.0%, 43.3%, 43.3%, 50.7% and 50.7%; promoted in rounds 1 and 3
claims.source: Tessera’s continuous-tuning record: one local GPU, one seed per configuration. Rounds 2 and 4 did not beat the champion, so the pre-registered rule kept it.

claims.number: Llama 3.2 3B, rounds 0 to 2 on the same test: exact match 52.0%, 72.7% and 79.3%; promoted in round 1, round 2 kept out by the schema guard, rounds 3 and 4 not run
claims.source: The same loop, test and rule. Round 2’s schema validity fell 0.025 against a 0.02 limit. Training then stopped until there is more checked data.

claims.number: Promoted gains, with paired bootstrap 95% CIs: 1B round 1 +31.3 points (+22.0 to +40.7), round 3 +7.3 (+0.7 to +14.7); 3B round 1 +20.7 (+12.0 to +29.3)
claims.source: The promotion decisions in Tessera’s continuous-tuning record: 55 rows better and 8 worse in the 1B’s round 1, 20 and 9 in its round 3, and 40 and 9 in the 3B’s round 1.

claims.number: 63 owned examples: typed values written as strings fell from 8.3% to 0% of calls, and type correctness rose from 37.5% to 94.2% (1B, round 1)
claims.source: The frozen-test diagnostics for the unchanged 1B and its round 1 adapter, in Tessera’s continuous-tuning record.

claims.number: Llama 3.2 3B (Hybrid LoRA + Compact Pointer): exact recall 64.2% to 91.7% on a 120-row test with a 38.5-token pointer, cutting shim tokens by 91.0% vs a 427.6-token BM25 shim (8 of 8 reload check)
claims.source: Local RTX 3060 LoRA-as-Memory paired with a 1-line compact pointer for live post-training delta Task Objects; made-up data only, nothing admitted or deployed.

claims.number: Llama 3.2 1B (Herma Shim Router): full route exact match 26.7% to 98.3% on a 120-row 5-action test (vs 10.0% zero-shot 1B), with 100.0% contributor-privacy refusal recall and 0.0% false refusals
claims.source: Local RTX 3060 1B edge router adapter classifying direct reply, Task-Object injection, task decomposition, frontier synthesis, and contributor-tier privacy refusal.

claims.number: Muse Glimmer 30B: exact match 93.3% to 99.3% on a fresh 150-row test, +6.0 points, 95% CI +2.0 to +10.7; 10 rows improved, 1 regressed
claims.source: QLoRA on free cloud GPUs, October 29, 2026. The fresh test was built after training, and its hashes were registered before scoring.

claims.number: Muse Glimmer 30B: promotion rule 12 of 12 checks passed; a fresh reload matched 8 of 8 regenerated rows
claims.source: The rule, tool-call-specialist.promotion version 1, was fixed before scoring and returned promote_candidate. Nothing has been promoted or admitted, and the adapter weights are not published.

claims.number: Muse Glimmer 30B: valid JSON 96.7% to 100.0%, correct refusals 97.3% to 99.3%; 0 test rows match the 511 training rows
claims.source: No exact, request-level or held-out-family match against the training rows. Against the older test set, 54 rows share only a request shape.

claims.number: Muse Glimmer 30B on the frozen development test: 87.3% to 98.7%
claims.source: The test used while developing the runs. It served more than one run, so the fresh test is the one that decides.

claims.number: Muse Glimmer 30B (LoRA-as-Memory): closed-book exact match 0.0% to 62.5% on a pre-registered 120-row test with 0 shim tokens (+33.3 points vs 222.3-token BM25 shim, 2.28 times faster, 8 of 8 reload check)
claims.source: QLoRA on two free Kaggle T4 GPUs, October 31, 2026: closed-book Task-Object recall and multi-step workflow synthesis without runtime context injection. Promoted candidate only; nothing has been admitted or deployed.

claims.number: Memory, path-statistics and routing-weights learners: implemented and tested
claims.source: Tessera’s execution-learning record. Local tests are not evidence that any learner improves real work; that needs the evaluations each learner names, on real permitted runs.

claims.number: Tuning on opted-in, verified, rights-cleared real runs
claims.source: The training export is a proposed design in Tessera’s execution-learning record. Nothing exports data from real runs yet.

claims.number: Muse Glimmer 30B QLoRA on Kaggle’s two free T4 GPUs: 64 training steps in 83 minutes, on 511 rows we wrote
claims.source: The 511-row run record: 64 steps and 4,997.5 seconds of training, with each stage, library version and the peak memory of both GPUs recorded. The whole job took 8,789.5 seconds. The notebooks themselves aren’t public yet.

claims.number: Llama 3.2 1B and 3B on one RTX 3060 12 GB: about 46 and 51 GPU-minutes, with no provider calls and no spending
claims.source: Tessera’s continuous-tuning record: rounds 0 to 4 and a serving check for the 1B, and rounds 0 to 2 for the 3B. The GPU is owned, and its electricity is not metered.

claims.number: Another key tried to read everything the 1B rounds wrote: all 303 reads were denied
claims.source: A final sweep after the 1B rounds: another principal tried to read 115 private records, 133 blob chunks and 55 execution runs. After the 3B rounds, all 193 such reads were denied too.

claims.number: The 150-row tests are small
claims.source: Tessera’s continuous-tuning record: with the disagreement these runs showed, a 150-row test detects a true 5-point gain only about 31% of the time, and 80% power needs about 560 rows.

claims.number: SIRA Self-Learning RAG + Herma Shims: Recall@1 23.3% to 100.0% across 60 queries over 79 seed packs (MRR 0.341 to 1.000 in 1.0 round, 82.8% token reduction, 0.30 ms retrieval, 10 compiled shims at 0.026 ms, 10 of 10 independent reviews)
claims.source: Offline standard-library evaluation over the 79-pack library: RARTF noun enrichment, analogy-aware cross-domain indexing, MR-Search adaptive reflection, and DGM-H independent verification (409 self-approval rejected).

claims.number: Meta ARE 4D Scenario Matrix (1,000 Episodes): 32.5% stakeholder-blocked vs 67.5% safely approved (15.1% direct plus 52.4% human-partitioned) across 1,000 4D scenarios spanning 25 domains
claims.source: Deterministic Latin-hypercube evaluation over 10^12 addressable 4D tuples (persona, environment, method, stakeholder constraint), separating direct agent work, human-partitioned drafts, and stakeholder-blocked escalations.

claims.number: Learning from live traffic
claims.source: Rounds start on demand today. A schedule that only enqueues the tick verb, and the export of real runs for training, are designed, not built.
